paper_metadata.title: Comparative Performance Analysis of Quantum Machine Learning Architectures for Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: The paper compares three gate-based quantum ML classifiers (VQC, SQNN, EQNN) for credit card fraud detection on balanced BankSim and ULB European datasets using 4–6 qubit circuits and Qiskit simulators. VQC achieves the best performance on the European dataset with an F1-score of 0.88 (Z feature map + Pauli Two Design ansatz), while SQNN performs best on BankSim with an F1-score of 0.85 (Z feature map + Real Amplitudes). EQNN performs significantly worse, with maximum F1-scores of 0.59 (BankSim) and 0.52 (European).

experiments.description: Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) for credit card fraud detection on BankSim and European datasets, evaluated across multiple feature maps and ansatz configurations.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are encoded via quantum feature maps (Pauli, ZZ, Z) into 4- or 6-qubit circuits; exact qubit-to-feature mapping not fully specified.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize cross-entropy loss for binary fraud classification.

problem_instance.description: Binary credit card fraud detection on two datasets: BankSim and a European credit card fraud dataset.
problem_instance.dataset_name: BankSim, European credit card fraud dataset

dataset_specification.BankSim: 594,643 records over 180 simulation steps; 587,443 regular payments and 7,200 fraudulent transactions; balanced to 492 fraud and 492 non-fraud samples via random undersampling.
dataset_specification.European: ULB credit card fraud dataset; 284,807 transactions; 492 fraud cases; 28 PCA-transformed features plus Time and Amount; balanced to 492 fraud and 492 non-fraud samples via random undersampling.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random undersampling to balance classes 50/50; BankSim categorical fields numerically encoded; ZipCodeOrigin and ZipMerchant removed; European dataset reduced with PCA; MinMaxScaler applied to scale features to [0,1]; 80/20 train-test split.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance evaluated on test set using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and loss; ANOVA used for statistical validation; robustness tested under five quantum noise types.

noise_model.noise_type: amplitude damping, bit flip, depolarizing, phase damping, phase flip

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random undersampling, categorical encoding, PCA for European dataset, MinMax scaling, train-test split.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement outputs used for classification; metrics computed on test set.

speedup_claims.conditions: under standard assumptions for parametrized quantum circuits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic complexity statement, not an empirical speedup; no proven quantum advantage is claimed.

speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as classical simulation complexity; not a measured runtime comparison.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d n) per forward pass; O(p log d n) gradient-based update under standard assumptions

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not_reported; experiments use 4–6 qubits simulated on QasmSimulator with shallow variational circuits
limiting_factors: No classical baseline experiments in the paper
Results obtained only via classical simulation
No runtime or scaling comparison with classical ML
Data encoding of classical features into quantum states

notes: QasmSimulator is explicitly named; no real QPU device is reported.
Circuit depth is not explicitly given; only feature-map/ansatz repetitions and qualitative convergence plots are reported, so depth remains null.
The paper gives asymptotic complexity for parametrized quantum circuits and classical simulation, but does not claim a proven speedup.
The paper compares only quantum ML architectures (VQC, SQNN, EQNN) and does not experimentally benchmark against classical ML models.
Authors discuss classical literature but provide no direct runtime or accuracy comparison demonstrating quantum advantage.
